SegmentCost=$69,000,000 is corroborated by TWO independent figures that round to the same number: Texas Energy Report states 'about $69 million', and EIA's register carries Cost (millions)=68.9 -- a <0.2% variance, clearly the same underlying FERC-filed cost estimate reported to one more significant figure by EIA. Given a 12-inch line moving 275 MMcf/d over 24.7 miles is plausible but on the small side for that throughput (FGT's other laterals of similar length run 20-36 in for comparable or smaller volumes per the EIA register), this is flagged as an open caveat, not a disagreement -- no evidence either supports or contradicts 12 in.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently codes this segment as StartPrefecture/District=Matagorda County, StartState/Province=Texas -> EndState/Province=Louisiana. TWO independent sources put the flow, and the state coding, the other way around. (1) Texas Energy Report states explicitly: 'Florida Gas wants to build and operate the pipeline from proposed two receipt points and one existing receipt point in LOUISIANA to two delivery points on FGT's system along the TEXAS Gulf Coast' -- i.e. gas enters in Louisiana and is delivered into Texas, the opposite direction of GEM's Start(TX)->End(LA) coding. (2) EIA's own register uses the same Start/End convention GEM does ('Beg_State' / 'End_State') and lists this exact row as Beg_State='LA', End_State='TX' -- again the reverse of GEM. Two independent sources agreeing with each other, and disagreeing with GEM, on which end is the origin, is a real attribution defect, not a rounding/labeling nuance -- worth a concern flag even though it doesn't touch existence. It's plausible 'Matagorda County' is nonetheless the correct TEXAS-side (delivery) location name and just needs its Start/End role flipped, rather than being wrong itself, but I could not confirm the county from either source (neither TER nor EIA names counties), so I'm not proposing a replacement value -- only flagging the direction defect for a researcher with FERC-docket access (or the FGT system map) to resolve precisely.
